svg.title: Differential rotation of the Sun
svg.desc: Animated diagram of the Sun's differential rotation. A chain of markers starts on one meridian of the solar disc; over 9 days (sped up, day counter shown) the equator carries its markers farthest, so the chain shears into a curve. Rates are the sidereal fit ω = 14.713 − 2.396 sin²φ − 1.787 sin⁴φ degrees per day (Snodgrass & Ulrich 1990): period 24.5 days at 0°, 24.8 days at 15°, 25.7 days at 30°, 27.5 days at 45°, 30.2 days at 60°, 33.0 days at 75°, 34.2 days at 90°. So the equator turns in about 25 days and the poles in about 34–35. Sunspots (drawn at 0°, ±15°, ±30°) only appear within about ±35°; higher latitudes are measured from magnetic features and helioseismology. Seen from the orbiting Earth the equatorial (synodic) period is 26.2 days. The solar equator is drawn edge-on (B₀ = 0).
svg.text: The Sun's equator outruns its poles
shaded: sunspot belt · ● sunspot ○ magnetic tracer · Snodgrass & Ulrich 1990
seen from the moving Earth, the equator takes 26.2 d (synodic)
